premises.text: Students learn much more from peers than from professors or video content, yet edtech is overwhelmingly top-down
premises.evidence_span: Studies show that peers learn seven times more from each other than they do from any video content, anything hands down from the professors. Yet 99% of all educational technology is built for top down

premises.text: Facebook and Blackboard are poor tools for finding your course and classmates when you need academic help
premises.evidence_span: on Facebook, you can't find your course, your classmates. You can't really, and you don't really want to do that through things like Blackboard. It's not as user-friendly

premises.text: Study Hall is a peer platform with study-buddy recommendations, shared course spaces, notes, live sessions, and gamified ratings
premises.evidence_span: We built an incredibly easy way to connect with your classmates, find your peers, and study in real time

premises.text: Monetization centers on a peer-to-peer marketplace for study materials and partnerships with online learning institutions
premises.evidence_span: We built a peer-to-peer marketplace. We can partner with online universities where people go watch videos, but what do you do next?

value.text: Capture peer-to-peer learning so students connect with classmates and ease academic life
value.evidence_span: We're capturing the power of peer-to-peer learning

causal_links.evidence_span: peers learn seven times more from each other
connect with your classmates and make your academic life easier

notes: Pilots at elite schools and honor society partnership treated as traction/GTM evidence, not core theory premises. Algorithm, notes, marketplace listing UI folded into platform vs money split: marketplace+partners kept as commercial module because speaker answers 'how could we make money' with those. Pitch truncates mid-monetization slide.
